market_holds: Spot $31.10 at the 18:08 UTC seal. The options price an event move of about 11.0% (3-day straddle 11.4%, ATM IV 135%), and 25-delta put skew is +15 vol points, so the market is paying for downside (sealed baseline). The last 7 reactions have a median absolute move of 12.1% and went both ways: +20.2% Nov-25, -6.3% Feb-26, +14.8% Jun-26, -17.0% Aug-26. Each one followed EPS against consensus plus the next-quarter guide. The stock is -24% since the pre-August-print close of $40.83 and -8.5% since the post-print close of $33.91. That is in line with HVT (-12%) and FLXS (-9%), better than ETD (-29%) and worse than SPY (-4.8%). Over the last 20 sessions LZB is +6.4% while HVT is -12.8%, ETD -20.2%, FLXS -15.5% and SPY -4.8%. That gap is mostly LZB recovering from its own 10-21 low of $28.68 on sector up-days (10-22, 11-04), not company news. There has been no LZB 8-K since August (EDGAR). Consensus Q2 EPS is about $0.48 on revenue of about $507M, which is the midpoint of the company's own guide ($500-520M, adj. op margin 4-5.5%, -1% to +2% ex-casegoods). Estimates were cut after August (Sidoti Q2 from $0.73 to $0.48), and FY27 consensus was $2.54 as of 10-17 (chartmill via search snippet), -14.5% over 3 months. Short interest is about 4.9% of float with 2-3 days to cover, so positioning is not crowded.
view: This print looks like a guide-midpoint quarter for a stock that already reset 17% in August, and the inputs point slightly up on sales but not clearly on margin or the Q3 guide. On sales, the retail backlog built in Q1: written sales were +16% against delivered +10%, written same-store sales +3%, and customer deposits rose from $77.9M to $92.0M (10-Q). That backlog delivers in Q2. The comparison is easy, because last year's Q2 written same-store sales were -2%. Counterparties and peers covering Aug-Oct are flat to modestly positive. Census furniture-store sales for Aug-Oct are +3.2% y/y against -1.2% for May-Jul, though two-year stacks are flat at about 2-3%. Wayfair calls the category flat. Bassett's company-owned written sales were +4.4%, with a strong Labor Day, and its wholesale orders +7.9%. Flexsteel's orders were +5% and its backlog +8%. Haverty's comparable written sales slowed to +2.3% (Aug-Sep +1.7%), and Ethan Allen's retail orders were -1.2% (October +0.3%). The wholesale peers argue that LZB's own wholesale (-5% ex-casegoods in Q1, 'improving through the quarter, Q2 backlog solid') can do better than in Q1. Against that, margin is where LZB missed last time (3.9% against a 4-5.5% guide). Q2 carries known friction: the Mexico SLRC plant closed at the end of Q1, Joybird production is moving to US plants, the 110bp warranty benefit from last year does not repeat, and Labor Day advertising and the brand rollout add cost. Any IEEPA refund help is likely to be stripped out by the market, as it was for Haverty's (-11% on 11-05). The furniture tape has punished both recent peer prints (HVT -11%, ETD -11%). Q3 (Nov-Jan) faces last year's $542M and 6.1% margin, which included casegoods. I cannot see where consensus sits for Q3, and the guide is what the stock will trade on. Net: a slight lean up on the top line and retail delivery, no visible edge on the deciding guide or margin line, and a stock that is neither crowded nor run up on its own news.

recommendation.reason: Retail backlog conversion and better wholesale orders at mid-market peers (Flexsteel, Bassett) make a top-line outcome at or above the guide midpoint slightly more likely than not. But consensus already sits at that midpoint, and margin is where LZB missed last time. The stock will trade on the Q3 guide, and I could find no dated evidence that places it against consensus. There is no mechanism strong enough to reach 65%.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q3 guide whose midpoint sits clearly below last year's ex-divestiture base (roughly sales under $520M, or an adj. op margin range starting below 5%), or a Q2 adj. op margin below the 4% low end once tariff refunds are stripped. Either would repeat the August pattern down. Written same-store sales of mid-single digits or better, with October strongest, would tip it up.

self_critique: The case for down: furniture prints are being sold hard this month (HVT, ETD, RH weak), and the market strips refunds. LZB missed its own margin guide last quarter with friction still building (Mexico closure, Joybird move), and put skew says the market fears that again. A cautious Q3 guide in a soft tape could give another double-digit drop. The case for up: estimates are already at the guide midpoint, the comparison is easy (-2% written SSS last year), retail backlog is in hand, and the stock is near its 52-week low, so an in-line print with steady written trends could pop as in Nov-25. Both are plausible, which is why I stay near 50.
approach_notes: P6's run-in decomposition helped: it showed the 20-day outperformance was sector up-days and mean reversion, not company news, so it gave no fade signal. P7's 'estimate the line from inputs' was limited here because the deciding Q3 guide has no visible consensus, and the peer inputs conflict.
